- Coin (km 61) hosted the start of stage 13 in 2017: MatteoTrentin won in Tomares with Gianni Moscon in second place
- Yunquera (km 88.2) saw Ben O’Connor win stage 6 of La Vuelta 24 and take La Roja from Primoz Roglic
- Ronda (km 122.6) saw John Degenkolb win stage 5 of La Vuelta 14
- Estepona (km 186.1) saw Dietrich Thurau claim the first leader’s jersey of the 1976 edition, before witnessing victories from José De Cauwer (1976) and Jaan Kirsipuu (1998).
As for Malaga (km 27.4), it first appeared on the map of La Vuelta in 1936, the second edition of the race. Belgium’s Gustaf Deloor took his fifth stage win, the second that year, and went on to win La Vuelta for the second time in a row. More recently, Malaga hosted the Gran Salida of the 2018 edition. - Coin (km 61) hosted the start of stage 13 in 2017: MatteoTrentin won in Tomares with Gianni Moscon in second place
- Yunquera (km 88.2) saw Ben O’Connor win stage 6 of La Vuelta 24 and take La Roja from Primoz Roglic
- Ronda (km 122.6) saw John Degenkolb win stage 5 of La Vuelta 14
- Estepona (km 186.1) saw Dietrich Thurau claim the first leader’s jersey of the 1976 edition, before witnessing victories from José De Cauwer (1976) and Jaan Kirsipuu (1998).
As for Malaga (km 27.4), it first appeared on the map of La Vuelta in 1936, the second edition of the race. Belgium’s Gustaf Deloor took his fifth stage win, the second that year, and went on to win La Vuelta for the second time in a row. More recently, Malaga hosted the Gran Salida of the 2018 edition. - Coin (km 61) hosted the start of stage 13 in 2017: MatteoTrentin won in Tomares with Gianni Moscon in second place
- Yunquera (km 88.2) saw Ben O’Connor win stage 6 of La Vuelta 24 and take La Roja from Primoz Roglic
- Ronda (km 122.6) saw John Degenkolb win stage 5 of La Vuelta 14
- Estepona (km 186.1) saw Dietrich Thurau claim the first leader’s jersey of the 1976 edition, before witnessing victories from José De Cauwer (1976) and Jaan Kirsipuu (1998).

- Coin (km 61) hosted the start of stage 13 in 2017: MatteoTrentin won in Tomares with Gianni Moscon in second place
- Yunquera (km 88.2) saw Ben O’Connor win stage 6 of La Vuelta 24 and take La Roja from Primoz Roglic
- Ronda (km 122.6) saw John Degenkolb win stage 5 of La Vuelta 14
- Estepona (km 186.1) saw Dietrich Thurau claim the first leader’s jersey of the 1976 edition, before witnessing victories from José De Cauwer (1976) and Jaan Kirsipuu (1998).
As for Malaga (km 27.4), it first appeared on the map of La Vuelta in 1936, the second edition of the race. Belgium’s Gustaf Deloor took his fifth stage win, the second that year, and went on to win La Vuelta for the second time in a row. More recently, Malaga hosted the Gran Salida of the 2018 edition. - Coin (km 61) hosted the start of stage 13 in 2017: MatteoTrentin won in Tomares with Gianni Moscon in second place
- Yunquera (km 88.2) saw Ben O’Connor win stage 6 of La Vuelta 24 and take La Roja from Primoz Roglic
- Ronda (km 122.6) saw John Degenkolb win stage 5 of La Vuelta 14
- Estepona (km 186.1) saw Dietrich Thurau claim the first leader’s jersey of the 1976 edition, before witnessing victories from José De Cauwer (1976) and Jaan Kirsipuu (1998).
